ShimuraVarieties.summary: The libraries contain only GL₂-specific substrate: Mathlib's arithmetic subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) acting properly discontinuously on ℍ, cusps, congruence subgroups, ideles and finite étale algebras. Tau Ceti adds SL₂ strong approximation modulo N, abstract Hecke rings with associativity, the level-one ring ℂ[E₄,E₆], linear-algebraic Hodge structures, abelian varieties and the class-formation framework. Everything the roadmap actually constructs is missing: adelic Shimura varieties and their complex structure, neat levels, Baily–Borel, Borel extension, reflex norms and canonical models, CM theory, the Hodge/abelian-type and Milne descent arguments, and the scheme-level modular-curve comparison.

targets.target: Arithmeticity and commensurability of Γ = G(ℚ)₊ ∩ gKg⁻¹ for a reductive ℚ-group G and compact open K ⊂ G(𝔸_f)
targets.note: Commensurability is Mathlib's general group-theoretic notion, but "arithmetic" is defined only for subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) commensurable with SL(2,ℤ). Tau Ceti proves that finite-index subgroups of SL_n(ℤ) are commensurable with SL_n(ℤ) in GL_n(ℚ), with integral positive-determinant matrices in the commensurator. Nothing attaches an arithmetic group to a compact open level of a reductive ℚ-group.

targets.target: Reduction-theory inputs: rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite arithmetic coverings and finiteness of G(ℚ)\G(𝔸_f)/K
targets.note: Only the SL(2,ℤ) fundamental domain and the GL₁ cases of component finiteness (finite class and ray class groups) exist. There are no Siegel sets, no rational parabolics of a general group and no general finiteness of adelic double cosets.

targets.target: Hermitian-domain and effective-action specialization (the action of G^ad(ℚ)⁺ ∩ Γ on X⁺ with its kernel removed)
targets.note: Neither library defines Hermitian symmetric domains, Shimura data or effective arithmetic actions.

targets.target: Existence of neat congruence subgroups
targets.note: Neatness is not defined anywhere; no torsion-freeness theorem for Γ(N), N ≥ 3, was found either.

targets.target: Properly discontinuous action of the effective arithmetic groups on X⁺
targets.note: Proved only on ℍ: arithmetic subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) and discrete subgroups of SL(2,ℝ) act properly discontinuously, and proper discontinuity is commensurability-invariant. Nothing covers a general Hermitian symmetric domain.

targets.target: Connected-component decomposition Sh_K(ℂ) ≅ ⊔ Γ_g\X⁺ as an analytic isomorphism, independent of representatives
targets.note: There is no adelic double quotient G(ℚ)\(X × G(𝔸_f))/K in either library, even for GL₂.

targets.target: Strong approximation for semisimple simply connected groups with a noncompact factor
targets.note: Only the elementary SL₂ form exists: SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/N) is surjective, including along a coprime level. There is no adelic strong approximation for simply connected groups.

duplicates.note: D5 also defines neatness, the arithmetic subgroup attached to a compact open level and a connected component, and the effective arithmetic action.
ALS.0 proves the finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic Γ-components, proper discontinuity and freeness at neat level, for general reductive groups.
AA.3 owns the reduction theory V0 consumes: Siegel sets and finiteness of G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/K.
AA.4 develops strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups, the input V0 restricts to.

targets.target: Topology and complex-analytic structure on the double quotient G(ℚ)\(X × G(𝔸_f))/K
targets.note: There is no complex structure on any arithmetic quotient, not even Γ\ℍ. Tau Ceti has only the local model: a disc modulo a finite rotation group is a disc.

targets.target: Level maps and Hecke translations [x,a] ↦ [x,ag] from level K to g⁻¹Kg, agreeing with the quotient formulas
targets.note: There are no finite-level Shimura varieties to map between.

targets.target: Covering and finite étale analytic properties of level maps at neat levels
targets.note: Mathlib proves the general topological input: the quotient map of a properly discontinuous action is a covering map on the free locus. It is not applied to level maps, and there is no analytic finite étale notion.

targets.target: Effective deck group of a normal level inclusion K′ ⊂ K, a quotient of K/K′
targets.note: No deck-group calculation for arithmetic quotients exists.

targets.target: Hecke correspondence through K ∩ gKg⁻¹ with both maps and its composition law, independent of coefficient sheaves
targets.note: Only the algebraic shadow exists: Hecke coset modules of double cosets with the convolution product and its mixed-level associativity (Shimura, Chapter 3). The geometric correspondence Sh_{K∩gKg⁻¹} ⇉ Sh_K is absent.

duplicates.note: ALS.3 constructs the same two finite-level maps through K∩gKg⁻¹ and the resulting Hecke correspondences, on cochain complexes.
AA.4 constructs finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, their degrees, and the Cartesian diagrams of Hecke correspondences.

targets.target: Rational boundary components and their incidence
targets.note: Only the GL₂ case exists: cusps of arithmetic subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) are the points of ℙ¹(ℚ). There are no boundary components of a general Hermitian domain.

targets.target: Satake topology, and compactness of the arithmetic quotient of the partial compactification
targets.note: Neither the Satake topology nor any compactification of Γ\ℍ exists.

targets.target: Analytic structure and normality of the compactified quotient
Automorphic forms with their growth condition, and the Koecher principle where used
targets.note: Only elliptic modular forms exist, with holomorphy at the cusps built into the definition. There are no automorphic forms on a general Hermitian domain and no Koecher principle.

targets.target: Finite generation of the graded ring of automorphic forms, and separation by sufficiently high weights
targets.note: Only level one is done: Tau Ceti proves that the level-one modular forms form ℂ[E₄,E₆]. Finite generation at other levels, and separation of points, are absent.

targets.target: Projective realization and Chow algebraization
targets.note: There is no Chow theorem and no analytic GAGA in either library.

targets.target: Algebraic open variety, projective normal minimal compactification, boundary stratification, and algebraicity of level maps

duplicates.note: C4 states the projective-realization → Chow algebraization step of Baily–Borel as its own export.
C6 proves the Koecher extension theorem needed for Hilbert sections, one case of the Koecher step V2 must justify.
C5 proves graded-section finite generation and projectivity of the integral PEL minimal compactification, the integral analogue of V2's construction.
R12.3 constructs the compactified modular curve with its cusp parameters, the GL₂ instance of the minimal compactification.

targets.target: Extension of holomorphic maps from products of punctured discs into the arithmetic quotient (Borel extension)
targets.note: Neither library has Borel's extension theorem or even the big Picard theorem.

targets.target: Borel's algebraicity theorem (Milne Theorem 3.14 and Lemma 3.15)
Reduction of a general smooth algebraic source to quasi-projective charts, and descent of the algebraic maps
targets.note: The normal-crossings compactification input (R09.7d) is also absent: there is no resolution of singularities.

targets.target: Uniqueness of the algebraization at neat levels, and functoriality for morphisms of data
Extension to all levels by finite quotients, with the finite-quotient and normalization statements used in V8
targets.note: Neither library has quotients of schemes by finite groups.

targets.target: Reflex norm on ideles for a special pair (T,h)
targets.note: Mathlib has the idele group and idele class group of a number field. There are no algebraic tori over ℚ with cocharacters, special pairs or reflex norms.

targets.target: Comparison of the supplier's Artin normalization with Milne's, with a named conversion
targets.note: There is no global Artin reciprocity map for number fields. Tau Ceti has only the abstract class-formation framework of Artin–Tate.

targets.target: Definition of a canonical model over E(G,X), by the reciprocity law at special points and their fields of definition
Independence of the idele lifting a Galois automorphism
Finite-level torus models as finite étale schemes from the finite Galois sets given by reciprocity
targets.note: Mathlib has the category of finite étale algebras with its fibre functor, and its anti-equivalence with finite sets over a separably closed field. Galois descent to finite Gal(Ē/E)-sets and the torus models are absent.

targets.target: Functoriality of torus models and compatibility with the geometric double quotient
Density of special points and their Hecke translates

duplicates.note: CM.0 also constructs reflex norms on the torus/idele objects.

targets.target: Algebraization of polarized weight-one variations over smooth algebraic bases
targets.note: Tau Ceti has only linear-algebraic polarized weight-one Hodge structures (the Riemann bilinear relations). There are no variations of Hodge structure and no algebraization theorems.

targets.target: CM types, reflex types and reflex norms
targets.note: CM fields exist (Mathlib IsCMField, and Tau Ceti's multiquadratic CM-field material). CM types, reflex fields and reflex norms do not.

targets.target: Tate-module action on CM abelian varieties
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field and their endomorphism monoids. Tate modules of abelian varieties and CM structures are absent.

targets.target: Main theorem of complex multiplication: reduction at suitable primes, Shimura–Taniyama, polarizations and levels, full reciprocity law
The Siegel moduli model satisfies the canonical-model condition
targets.note: There are no Siegel moduli spaces in either library.

duplicates.note: CM.0 constructs CM types and reflex norms, which V5 also constructs.
M4 proves compatibility of the moduli Galois action with CM reciprocity and identifies the moduli pieces with canonical models, overlapping V5's Siegel canonical-model step.

targets.target: Canonical-model inheritance for a Shimura subdatum (Hodge type), with its special-point proof
Connected Shimura varieties, their adelic/Galois symmetry, and equivalence with the nonconnected formulation
Descent through central isogenies of derived groups and finite component quotients; abelian-type canonical models
targets.note: Tau Ceti has central isogenies of group schemes as general group theory. Nothing concerns Shimura varieties.

targets.target: Reduction to connected, simple, simply connected data
targets.note: Tau Ceti has simply connected semisimple group schemes as Hopf algebras. There are no Shimura data to reduce.

targets.target: The group as a restriction of scalars from a totally real field
targets.note: Totally real number fields exist in Mathlib; Weil restriction of algebraic groups does not exist in either library.

targets.target: Auxiliary totally real extension, splitting over a CM quadratic extension, and type-A₁ subdata with their compatibilities
Conjugated Shimura datum for an automorphism of ℂ, and algebraic comparison of the conjugated varieties compatible on A₁ subvarieties
Uniqueness giving the cocycle law, continuity of the descent datum, and effective quasi-projective descent to the reflex field
Level maps and Hecke correspondences over the reflex field, with analytic comparison and functoriality
Descent of the minimal compactifications to the reflex field
Sh_{K(N)}(GL₂, ℍ±) ≅ Y_full(N)_ℚ for N ≥ 3
targets.note: Neither library has modular curves as schemes, nor the moduli of elliptic curves with level structure.

targets.target: Determinant morphism equals the Weil-pairing morphism; fibre over ζ is Y(N,ζ), with analytification Γ(N)\ℍ
targets.note: Mathlib has the principal congruence subgroup Γ(N). The Weil pairing and the analytic quotient Γ(N)\ℍ as a complex curve are absent.

targets.target: Dictionary between row-basis actions and the adelic convention; Γ₁ and Γ₀ comparisons with fine/coarse qualifications
Comparison of minimal compactifications, cusp loci and Tate parameters

duplicates.note: R12.2 classifies full, Γ₁ and Γ₀ level structures under uniformisation, with the fine/coarse distinction and the determinant–root-of-unity identification that V8 restates.
M5 proves the genus-one comparison of Siegel moduli with #81, including the determinant/Weil-pairing convention.
C6 compares the generic-fibre minimal curve with ModularCurvesPartII R13.4a/R13.4b, the same comparison V8 states.
H5 identifies the F = ℚ Hilbert constructions with the modular-curve ones, overlapping V8's GL₂ comparison.
AA.5 identifies the GL₂/ℚ upper-half-plane component through ModularCurvesPartII uniformization.

targets.target: V8's level maps and functorial canonical-model comparisons for the general data of V7
targets.note: This depends on V7 and V8, neither of which exists.

SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCa.summary: The libraries have the number-field substrate R25.1 starts from: Mathlib's Minkowski discriminant bound, Hermite–Minkowski, Hermite finiteness, root discriminants, the different ideal with its tame exponent, and Tau Ceti's effective Hermite count. Missing: wild local different bounds, Odlyzko-type analytic bounds with certified numerics, and everything from R25.2 on, namely the Tate–Serre, Fontaine and Schoof nonexistence theorems, GL₂-type terminal cases and the base-case table. Neither library has global Galois representations with ramification conditions, reduction of abelian varieties, or ramification theory for finite flat group schemes.

targets.target: Local discriminant (different) upper bounds for torsion fields, with wild ramification retained
targets.note: The different-ideal theory exists: 𝔭^(e−1) ∣ 𝔇 (Mathlib), 𝔭 ∣ 𝔇 iff ramified, the exact tame exponent e−1 (Tau Ceti), and the discriminant as the norm of the different in towers. Missing: any wild upper bound (v(𝔇) ≤ e−1+v(e)), higher ramification groups for number fields, and Fontaine's bound for torsion of finite flat group schemes.

targets.target: Geometry-of-numbers (Minkowski) lower bound for |d_K| in terms of degree and signature, with root discriminants
targets.note: abs_discr_ge' is the Minkowski bound n^(2n)/((4/π)^(2r₂)·n!²) ≤ |d_K|, and abs_discr_ge its exponential form (4/9)(3π/4)^n for n > 1. Mathlib also defines the root discriminant.

targets.target: Analytic explicit-formula (Odlyzko-type) discriminant lower bounds, with certified numerical inequalities
targets.note: Neither library has Odlyzko/Poitou-type bounds or any Weil explicit formula for Dedekind zeta functions. Minkowski's bound is too weak for the torsion fields in the Tate and Fontaine arguments.

targets.target: Completeness of a finite exceptional list of number fields from the bound, and validation of the listed fields
targets.note: Hermite finiteness (Mathlib), an explicit upper bound on the number of fields of bounded discriminant, and discriminant computation from an integral basis (Tau Ceti) exist, as does Minkowski's theorem that every K ≠ ℚ ramifies. No certified enumeration or completeness proof for a specific list exists.

duplicates.note: R07.6 proves Fontaine's ramification bound for finite flat torsion and its normalized different bound, the local input R25.1 turns into discriminant bounds.
EffectiveBounds layer 2 owns the effective Hermite–Minkowski count of fields with bounded discriminant, used in R25.1's list-completeness step.

targets.target: Tate: no odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional mod-2 representation of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) unramified outside 2
targets.note: Neither library has Galois representations with ramification conditions. Only Minkowski's theorem that ℚ has no unramified extension, the degenerate input, is present.

targets.target: Serre: the mod-3 analogue, unramified outside 3
Treatment of soluble and nonsoluble images, and of larger coefficient fields F_{2^k}, F_{3^k}
Fontaine: no positive-dimensional abelian variety over ℚ with good reduction everywhere, in all dimensions
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field and Mathlib defines good reduction of a Weierstrass equation over a DVR. There is no reduction theory for abelian varieties, and not even the conductor-one elliptic case.

targets.target: Finite flat group-scheme, ramification and discriminant arguments for the torsion
targets.note: Tau Ceti has finite locally free commutative affine group schemes with Cartier duality over an affine base, but no ramification theory for their generic-fibre points.

targets.target: Conversion of the torsion restrictions into a contradiction
Schoof: no nonzero semistable abelian variety over ℚ with good reduction outside one prime p ∈ {2,3,5,7,13}
Classification and extension calculations for the finite flat group schemes over ℤ[1/p]
targets.note: Only the general category of finite locally free commutative group schemes with Cartier duality exists; no extension groups or classification.

targets.target: Global argument passing from torsion group schemes to the abelian variety
Geometric realisation of the weight-two compatible systems in the exact Snowden/source form, with good/semistable reduction verified
targets.note: Neither library has compatible systems, GL₂-type abelian varieties or their reduction.

targets.target: Local crystalline-to-ordinary calculations at the terminal weights
Reduction of each small-weight terminal case to a theorem of R25/R17/R21

duplicates.note: R33.4 constructs the semistable GL₂-type abelian variety in Snowden's form for the weight-6 terminal case, and does the characteristic-three ordinary calculation for weights 2 and 4.
R26.5 applies the R25 exclusions to each remaining base case after verifying dimension, field of definition and reduction set.

targets.target: Table of every base case used by R26 and R33: characteristic, weight, ramification, image, coefficient assumptions and proof supplier
targets.note: This is bookkeeping over theorems that do not yet exist.

targets.target: A separate local calculation for each exceptional transition, independent of the Serre theorem being initialised

duplicates.note: R26.5 must also list the finite set of exceptional characteristics and weights with their terminal theorems.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps.summary: Tau Ceti already has almost all of Layer 0: permutation triples, relabeling, monodromy and automorphism groups, the opposite-convention involution, full cycle data, the transposition step and sign identities, combinatorial χ ≤ 2 with genus, and orders with geometry type. It also has the Layer 2.1–2.2 ribbon-graph carrier with triple → dessin, and the inverse-class involution of 3.2. Several items the roadmap treats as unresolved supplier contracts are already there: Mathlib's IsCoveringMap.monodromyPerm is 5.3's monodromy homomorphism, and Tau Ceti's universal-cover classification supplies 6.2's associated cover of a π₁-set (no inverse), the general subgroup/deck/regular classification behind 6.3–6.5, and the profinite-completion fibre-functor theorem behind 12.6. Genuinely missing: passports, dessins → triples, the branch-point S₃-action, executable enumeration and the Frobenius formula, triangle groups, ℂ∖{0,1} with π₁ ≅ F₂ and van Kampen, and all of Layers 7–14 (compactification, Riemann-surface theory, algebraic Belyi pairs, Belyi's theorem, fields of moduli, ẑ and profinite powers, the branch-cycle and pro-ℓ theorems, faithfulness, LMFDB semantics).

targets.target: 0.1 Carrier PermutationTriple n (σinf·σ1·σ0 = 1): ofTwo, extensionality from two components, Fintype/DecidableEq, trivial triple, degree 0 and 1, transport, relation rotations
targets.note: Same relation and composition order as the roadmap. The Fintype, DecidableEq, One and Subsingleton (for Subsingleton (Fin n), covering n = 0, 1) instances are unnamed instances in Basic.lean, lines 171–187.

targets.target: 0.1 Opposite-convention involution, preserving cycle types, monodromy groups, connectedness and automorphism groups
targets.note: Componentwise inversion, as a bijection onto the triples with σ0·σ1·σinf = 1.

targets.target: 0.2 Relabeling MulAction by simultaneous conjugation; isomorphism as a decidable orbit relation; IsoClass; compatibility with ofTwo and the involution; preservation of cycle data
targets.note: The MulAction and DecidableRel Equivalent instances are unnamed (Basic.lean lines 235, 273); cycleData_smul and isConnected_smul_iff give the preservation statements.

targets.target: 0.3 Monodromy group closure{σ0,σ1}: contains σinf, equals the closure of all three, conjugated by relabeling
0.4 IsConnected := n ≠ 0 ∧ pretransitive monodromy, with a decidability instance
targets.note: The definition includes the n ≠ 0 clause and is relabeling-invariant. No Decidable instance for IsConnected was found; Layer 3.1's isConnectedB is also absent.

targets.target: 0.4 Automorphism group = simultaneous centralizer; free action for connected triples, so its order divides n; conjugation under relabeling
targets.note: The freeness and divisibility statements assume only pretransitivity of the monodromy group. automorphismGroup_smul gives the conjugation.

targets.target: 0.5 Full cycle partitions (fixed points included), cycle counts, sum = n, comparison with Equiv.Perm.partition, conjugation/transport invariance
targets.note: Tau Ceti's cycleData uses Mathlib's Equiv.Perm.partition directly. The PolynomialGaloisGroups name fullCycleType also exists in Tau Ceti, as Equiv.Perm.fullCycleType, with conjugation and transport lemmas. The cycle count via cycleType is Mathlib's Equiv.Perm.parts_partition.

targets.target: 0.5 Transposition step lemma (merge/split of cycle counts) and sign identity sign σ = (−1)^(n − cycleCount σ)
targets.note: The right-multiplication forms (orbitCount_mul_swap_…) are also present.

targets.target: 0.6 Euler characteristic χ(t): parity, additivity over disjoint sums (with cycle-data concatenation and componentwise monodromy), χ ≤ 2 for connected triples by the transposition induction, and the junk-free genus
targets.note: disjointSum, cycleData_disjointSum and monodromyGroup_disjointSum_le are also present. The bound is proved combinatorially, as the roadmap requires.

targets.target: 0.6 Decomposition of any triple, up to relabeling, as the disjoint sum of its orbit restrictions, and the bound χ(t) ≤ 2·#orbits
targets.note: Only the forward construction and disconnectedness of disjoint sums exist; neither the orbit decomposition nor the general bound was found.

targets.target: 0.7 orderTriple = (orderOf σ0, orderOf σ1, orderOf σinf) = lcm of cycle partitions; GeometryType by exact rational comparison; invariance under relabeling and the involution
0.8 Named example suite: degree-one, cyclicTriple n, the 4z(1−z) triple, a disconnected sum, an isomorphic pair, torusTriple, the S₃ triple, each with invariants proved
targets.note: Tau Ceti has only two anonymous examples (z ↦ z³ and a disjoint sum of trivial covers) in EulerCharacteristic.lean; none of the named examples exists.

targets.target: 1.1 ConnectedTriple subtype with the restricted relabeling action
1.1 PassportSpec with admissibility and membership (conjugate monodromy, equal full cycle types), with invariance lemmas
1.2 Passport class sets and passportSize; the passport determines degree, genus, orderTriple and geometry type
1.3 Normalizer formulation: isomorphism classes ↔ N_{S_n}(G)-orbits of generating product-one triples in G³
1.4 Quotient triples from block systems, cycle-data refinement, IsPrimitive via IsPreprimitive, transitivity of quotients
targets.note: Mathlib has blocks and primitivity, and Tau Ceti has primitive actions from extremal blocks (GroupTheory/Perm/Blocks.lean), but nothing about triples.

targets.target: 1.5 passportOf : ConnectedTriple n → PassportSpec n with admissibility and its universal property
1.6 Label semantics at reference degrees n ≤ 11 through the nTj reference subgroups
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the nTj reference subgroups and label predicate only for degrees ≤ 5. The atlas's PolynomialGaloisGroups also stops at Layer 6 (n ≤ 5); the "Layer 7" the roadmap cites for n ≤ 11 does not exist. The passport-label predicate is absent.

duplicates.note: Owns the nTj label predicate that 1.6 interprets, but only for n ≤ 5, short of 1.6's n ≤ 11.

targets.target: 2.1 BipartiteRibbonGraph carrier with morphisms, isomorphisms, automorphism group, face permutation, connectedness, components, vertex degrees, Euler characteristic and degree sums
targets.note: The fields match the roadmap (universe-polymorphic rather than Type). Hom and Iso are present, and so are sum_blackDegree and sum_whiteDegree.

targets.target: 2.2 Triple → dessin: the graph of a triple, connected iff the triple is, faces ↔ cycles of σinf, equal Euler characteristics
targets.note: Defined for every n, not only n ≠ 0.

targets.target: 2.3 Dessin → triple via a numbering of the edges, well defined up to relabeling, with facePerm ↦ σinf
2.4 Equivalence of classifications (round trips; bijection of isomorphism classes of connected dessins and triples; automorphism groups)
targets.note: Only the triple → graph direction and its compatibility with relabeling exist.

targets.target: 2.5 Parity, χ ≤ 2 and genus for connected dessins, transported from Layer 0.6
targets.note: Holds for graphs of triples through eulerChar_ribbonGraph; it is not available for an arbitrary connected ribbon graph without 2.3–2.4.

targets.target: 2.6 The six branch-point operations with composite identities, the S₃-action on isomorphism classes and ordered passports, the dessin formulas, and agreement of the combinatorial, topological and algebraic actions
targets.note: No swap01, swap1Inf, rot or rotInv exists in the library.

targets.target: 2.7 Dessin examples of the Layer 0.8 suite
3.1 Executable enumeration: computable cycle decomposition with comparison theorem, isConnectedB, primitivity decision, enumeration Finsets of classes and passport fibres, decide-checked counts
targets.note: Only the Fintype and DecidableEq instances on triples and the decidable relabeling relation exist (unnamed instances, Basic.lean). Computed cycle types, Boolean connectedness and primitivity, and the class and passport Finsets are absent.

targets.target: 3.2 Inverse-class involution on ConjClasses G, with carrier (C⁻¹) = (carrier C)⁻¹ and equal class sizes
targets.note: The roadmap says this is "on no other roadmap"; Tau Ceti already has it (Algebra/Group/Conj.lean).

targets.target: 3.2 Product-one count = |Cinf|·structureConstant; character formula for structure constants; assembled Frobenius product-one formula; the S₃ worked check
targets.note: All inputs are present in Tau Ceti: structure constants, the class-sum central-character formula ω(K_C)·χ(1) = |C|·χ(g), and second orthogonality. The count conversion, the character formula for structure constants and the Frobenius formula are absent.

targets.target: 3.3 Generating-triple counts by strong downward recursion over the subgroup lattice
3.4 Counts to passport sizes: classesOfType, genCount, normalizer orbits, exact division formula with C_{S_n}(G), centralizer bound
targets.note: Mathlib has Burnside's lemma. Semiregularity of the centralizer is proved only for the monodromy group of a triple, not for an arbitrary pretransitive G. The passport-size formula is absent.

targets.target: 3.5 Complete tables for n ≤ 4 (1, 3, 7, 26 classes), every ordered passport of size 1, the degree-5 C₅ passport of size 3, and the database comparison
4.1 TriangleGroup a b c as a presented group, with universal property, rotation isomorphisms, elimination of z, and parameter 0
4.2 Triples with orders dividing (a,b,c) as permutation representations; classification of connected triples by transitive finite actions
4.3 Dividing/exact/surjective predicates and the necessary conditions n·(1/a+1/b+1/c−1) ≤ 2
4.4 Orbifold Euler characteristic; spherical classification with orders m, 2m, 12, 24, 60 (presentation comparisons and coset enumerations); Euclidean infiniteness by the affine representation
targets.note: Tau Ceti can recognize a group generated by two non-identity involutions as dihedral. There are no triangle groups, coset enumeration or finiteness classification.

targets.target: 4.5 Hyperbolic infiniteness via the SL(2,ℝ) representation, the trigonometric lemma and the Fricke trace identity
targets.note: Mathlib only defines hyperbolic 2×2 matrices; the trace identity and the infinite-order consequence are absent.

targets.target: 4.6 Regular triples ↔ finite-index normal subgroups of the triangle group

duplicates.note: Constructs hyperbolic triangle groups from polygon reflections and proves discreteness and faithfulness, the geometric counterpart of 4.5's infiniteness.

targets.target: 5.1 U = ℂ∖{0,1} with its two-set cover, instances (T2, locally path-connected, path-connected, second countable, semilocally simply connected), open embedding into OnePoint ℂ, punctured-disc neighbourhoods, six anharmonic self-homeomorphisms
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the semilocal simple connectivity class and derives it from strong local contractibility, but no instance covers open subsets of ℂ. The space U and its structure are absent.

targets.target: 5.2 Peripheral loops γ0, γ1 and periph0/1/Inf, with the mob01 pointwise identities
5.3 monodromyHom : FundamentalGroup X x →* Equiv.Perm (p⁻¹{x}) with its value lemma and naturality in maps of covers
targets.note: Mathlib's monodromyPerm is exactly this homomorphism, with no ᵐᵒᵖ, although the roadmap plans to build it. Tau Ceti adds naturality in maps of covers.

targets.target: 5.3 Compatibility of monodromy with pullback of covers along f : Y → X
targets.note: Neither library defines pullbacks of covering spaces.

targets.target: 5.4 Punctured convex domains: radial deformation retraction, π₁(ℂ∖{0}) ≅ ℤ from the exponential cover, transport, and identification with the winding number
targets.note: Present: π₁ of the circle ≅ ℤ (Tau Ceti), the exponential quotient covering and the quotient-cover π₁ comparison (Mathlib). Absent: π₁(ℂ∖{0}), the retraction and the winding-number invariant.

targets.target: 5.5 Two-open Seifert–van Kampen with simply connected intersection, with the named canonical map vanKampenLift, its bijectivity and vanKampenEquiv (supplier contract)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves only the generation half of the groupoid van Kampen theorem and uniqueness of functors out of the fundamental groupoid. The pushout/free-product theorem is absent.

targets.target: 5.6 π₁(U,b) ≃* FreeGroup (Fin 2) with of 0 ↦ periph0, of 1 ↦ periph1, and corollaries
5.7 Basepoint change: the peripheral conjugacy classes are independent of path and basepoint
targets.note: The basepoint-change isomorphisms exist; the peripheral statement needs 5.2 and 5.6.

targets.target: 5.8 periphInf is the clockwise radius-3 loop, i.e. the peripheral class at ∞
